claims.text: Additive manufacturing combined with thermomechanical treatment can refine the grain size and morphology of refractory high-entropy alloys.
The resulting refined microstructure increases the strength of refractory high-entropy alloys under high-temperature and irradiation conditions.
The resulting refined microstructure increases the ductility of refractory high-entropy alloys under high-temperature and irradiation conditions.
Grain refinement increases resistance to irradiation-induced damage in refractory high-entropy alloys.
The grain-refinement intervention maintains thermal stability while improving mechanical performance.
The grain-refinement intervention maintains irradiation stability while improving mechanical performance.
Impurities and trace elements may affect the properties of the treated refractory high-entropy alloys.
Improved mechanical performance may trade off against thermal or irradiation stability.
